content.text:
Checking the diagonals from the cyan cell at (5,4): I find hits at distance 3 up-left, distance 4 up-right, and distance 2 down-left, with nothing along the down-right diagonal.

The closest hit is down-left at distance 2, landing on a color-3 component spanning (7,1),(7,2),(7,3),(8,3),(8,4). I fill the path cells with cyan, then add black outline cells around each target cell, and build out rows 6-9 of the output grid accordingly.

Checking the diagonal neighbors from cyan's position at (4,2), the closest match found is at distance 1, with (-1,-1) being the first candidate encountered at that minimal distance.

So the target is the 4-colored component made of cells (3,1),(4,1),(5,1),(6,1),(6,2), all orthogonally connected with no diagonal spans. I'm now tracing which orthogonal neighbors of these cells are black, so I can outline them with cyan, then updating the grid rows accordingly to reflect the new cyan border cells around this component.
